questions.question:
A right circular cone is inscribed in a cube of side 9 cm occupying the maximum space possible. What is the ratio of the volume of the cube to the volume of the cone?

(Take π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
Given:

Side of the cube = 9 cm

Concept used:

Diameter = Radius × 2

The volume of a cube = (Measure of side)³ unit³

The volume of a cone = π/3 × Radius² × Height

Calculation:

Since the cone is occupying the maximum space within the cube, the diameter of the base and the height of the cone must be equal to the side of the cube.

Hence, the radius of the base of the cone inscribed in the cube = 9/2 cm and height = 9 cm

Now, 

The volume of the cone = π/3 × (9/2)² × 9 cm²

The volume of the cube = 9³ cm³

Hence, the ratio of their volume = 

9³ : π/3 × (9/2)2 × 9 

⇒ 42 : 11

**∴ The ratio of the volume of the cube to the volume of the cone is 42 : 11.**

questions.question: Jack takes thrice as much time as Peter and twice as much as Justin to finish a work; working together they can finish the work in 15 days. The time (in days) Justin will take to finish the work alone is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Jack takes thrice as much time as Peter and twice as much as Justin to finish a work.

Working together they can finish the work in 15 days. 

Concept used:

Efficiency and Time taken are inversely proportional.

Entire Work = Work done a day × Total time taken to finish (in days)

Calculation:

Let Jack does Q units of work a day.

Hence, Peter and Justin do 3Q and 2Q units of work a day.

Thus, the entire work = 15 × (Q + 3Q + 2Q) = 90Q units

Now, time taken by Justin to finish the work alone = 90Q ÷ 2Q = 45 days

**∴ Justin will take 45 days to finish the work alone.**

questions.question: Four solid cubes, each of volume 1728 cm³, are kept in two rows having two cubes in each row. They form a rectangular solid with square base. The total surface area (in cm²) of the resulting solid is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Four solid cubes, each of volume 1728 cm3, are kept in two rows having two cubes in each row.

Concept used:

The volume of a cube = (Length of its side)³

The total surface area of a cuboid = 2 × (LB + BH + LH) 

Where L = Length, B = Breadth, H = Height

Calculation:

Now, the length of each side of each cube = ³√1728 = 12 cm

Four cubes when arranged in two rows, thus,

Height = 12 cm

Breadth = (12 + 12) = 24 cm 

Length = (12 + 12) = 24 cm

Hence, total surface area of the resulting solid = (12 × 24 + 12 × 24 + 24 × 24) × 2 = 2304 cm²

**∴ The total surface area of the resulting solid is 2304 cm².**

The median is the middle value in a list ordered from smallest to largest.

The mean is equal to the total sum of a set of numbers when divided by the number of numbers in the set.

questions.question: P and Q are two towns. A man drives from P to Q at an average speed of 50 km/h. He stops at Q for 4 hours and then heads back to P at an average speed of 40 km/h following the same route. What is his average speed (in km/h correct to two decimal places) if he takes 22 hours for the entire trip?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average driving speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂) = (2 × 50 × 40) ÷ (50 + 40) = 400/9 km/h.

Total driving time = Total time − Stoppage time = 22 − 4 = 18 hours.

Total distance = Average driving speed × Total driving time = (400/9) × 18 = 800 km.

Average speed for the entire trip = Total distance ÷ Total time = 800 ÷ 22 = 36.36 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.36 km/h.**

questions.question: A girl cycles from A to B, a distance of 25 km in 2 hours 20 minutes. The road from A is a levelled road for 15 km and then it slopes down to B. The average speed of the girl on the levelled road is 10 km/h. Her average downhill speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 2 hr 20 min = 7/3 hours

Time spent on levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 3/2 hours

Remaining time for downhill = 7/3 − 3/2 = 5/6 hours

Downhill distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km

Downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 25 km

Total time = 2 hours 20 minutes = 2 + 20/60 = 7/3 hours

Distance of levelled road = 15 km

Speed on levelled road = 10 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3270e4b975079e534db4d53ee002e4e4e8e80b5b37a0dcff7ff82e8fb849886c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken to cover the levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 hours = 3/2 hours

⇒ Remaining distance (downhill) = Total distance − Distance of levelled road

⇒ Remaining distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km

⇒ Remaining time = Total time − Time on levelled road

⇒ Remaining time = 7/3 − 3/2 = (14 − 9) / 6 = 5/6 hours

⇒ Average downhill speed = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time

⇒ Average downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = (10 × 6) / 5 = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: A trader purchased 500 kg of sugar at Rs. 40 per kg. He sold 200 kg of it at a profit of 10% and 120 kg at a loss of 5%. At what rate per kg (in Rs., correct to 2 decimal places) should be sell the remaining sugar to gain 12% on his initial investment?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of 500 kg is Rs. 40 per kg.

He sold 200 kg of it at a profit of 10% and 120 kg at a loss of 5%.

Desired overall gain percentage = 12%

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price (1 + Gain Percentage/100)

Selling Price = Cost Price (1 - Loss Percentage/100)

Calculation:

Total desired revenue after the transaction = 500 × 40 × (1 + 12/100) = Rs. 22400

Total selling price of (200 + 120) i.e. 320 kg sugar = (200 × 40 × (1 + 10/100)) + (120 × 40 × (1 - 5/100)) = Rs. 13360

Remaining amount of sugar = 500 - 320 = 180 kg

Hence, the selling price of the remaining 180 kg sugar = (22400 - 13360) ÷ 180 ≈ Rs. 50.22

**∴ The remaining sugar should be sold at Rs. 50.22.**

questions.question: The price of a semi-precious stone weighing 48 g, is Rs. 2,30,400. It is broken into two pieces whose weights are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 7. If the price is proportional to the square of the weight, then the loss (in Rs.) incurred, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Weight of the original stone = 48 g

Price = Rs. 230400

The ratio of the weights of the broken pieces = 5 : 7

The price is proportional to the square of the weight

Concept used:

Ratio Proportion

Calculation: 

Let the constant be K.

According to the question,

48² × K = 230400

⇒ K = 100

Now,

Price of the first broken piece = 100 × {48 × 5/(5 + 7)}² = Rs. 40000

Price of the second broken piece = 100 × {48 × 7/(5 + 7)}2 = Rs. 78400

Hence, total loss incurred = (230400 - 40000 - 78400) = Rs. 1,12,000

**∴ The loss incurred is Rs. 1,12,000.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Ratio of weight of broken pieces = 5 : 7, total weight = 48 gm

∴ 5 = 20 gm and 7 = 28 gm

A/Q Price ∝ Sq. of weight

230400 = k × 48 × 48

Here k = 230400/48 = 4800 ⇒ 4800/48 = 100 = k

Also, 

Also for 20 gm weight, price = k × 20² = 40000

And for 28 gm weight, price = k × 28² = 78400

Since its broken into two pieces, loss = total cost - cost after breaking

Loss = 230400 - 40000 - 78400 = Rs. 1,12,000.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 8 days while B alone can do it in 12 days. They work together for 4 days and the remaining work is completed by C alone in 4 days. They are paid Rs. 7,200 for the completion of the entire work. The earnings of A, B and C, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Given:

A can do a piece of work in 8 days while B alone can do it in 12 days.

They work together for 4 days and the remaining work is completed by C alone in 4 days.

They are paid = Rs. 7200

Concept used:

Total work = Work done each day × Total Time Taken (in days)

Wage is distributed according to the ratio of the efficiencies.

Calculation:

LCM (8, 12, 2) = 24

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by them.

Hence, the total work = 24 units

Thus,

A does each day = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units

B does each day = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 units

Hence, C does each day = {24 - (3 + 2) × 4} ÷ 4 = 1 unit

Thus, ratio of efficiencies = 3 : 2 : 1

Hence,

Earning of A = 7200 × {3 over (3 + 2 + 1)} = Rs. 3600

Earning of B = 7200 × {2 over (3 + 2 + 1)} = Rs. 2400

Earning of C = 7200 × {1 over (3 + 2 + 1)} = Rs. 1200

**∴ A gets Rs. 3600, B gets Rs. 2400 and C gets Rs. 1200.**

questions.question: An employee gets two successive increments in his salary, as a result of which his salary becomes 2.5 times initial salary. What was his first percentage increment, if the second percentage increment was 4 times as high as the first?
questions.solution:
Given:

Final salary becomes 2.5 times initial salary.

Second percentage increment was 4 times as high as the first.

Concept used:

Result of two successive percentage increments of A% and B% = (A + B + AB/100)% 

Calculation:

Let the first percentage increment and the initial salary be Q% and Rs. P.

Thus, the second percentage increment = 4 × Q = 4Q%

Now, the final percentage increment in salary = {Q + 4 × Q + (4Q2/100)}%

His final salary = Rs. 2.5P

% increment = (2.5P - P)/P × 100% = 150%

According to the question, 

Q + 4 × Q + (4Q2/100) = 150

⇒ 500Q + 4Q2 = 15000

⇒ 4Q2 + 500Q - 15000 = 0

⇒ Q2 + 125Q - 3750 = 0

⇒ (Q - 25) (Q + 150) = 0

⇒ Q = 25 (taking the positive root only)

∴ The first percentage increment is 25%.

questions.question: The average age of a 10-person committee increases by 3 when three men aged 35 years. 48 years and 49 years are substituted by three women. The average age (in years) of the three women is:
questions.solution:
Given: 

The initial average of a 10-person committee increases by 3 when three men aged 35 years. 48 years and 49 years are substituted by three women.

Concept used:

Average = Total ÷ number of entities

Calculation:

Let the initial average age of the 10 committee members be Q years and the average age of three newly joined women be P years.

According to the question,

(10 × Q) - 35 - 48 - 49 + (3 × P) = 10 × (Q + 3)

⇒ P = 54

**∴ The average age of the three women is 54 years.**

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest. In how many years will it become 10 times of itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

The principal amount becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal amount be Rs. P and the rate of interest be R%.

According to the question,

(P × R × 12)/100 = 4P - P

⇒ R = 25%

Let the time taken for the principal amount to be 10 times of itself be T.

According to the question,

(P × 25 × T)/100 = 10P - P

⇒ T = 36

**∴ In 36 years the principal amount will become 10 times itself at the same rate. **
